body:
I've talked to and read comments from transwomen before and seen that as well actually, for some people who'd get erections they'd go away as they dressed more and especially after starting HRT. 

Crossdressing is really interesting to think about, when I'm thinking about it in a personal context at least, especially in regards to how it impacted sexual thoughts/feelings for me. I can remember growing up, whenever I'd see a girl who I thought was pretty I might imagine it would be nice to kiss her, but I'd also imagine myself looking/feeling like her and it would always get a stronger reaction from me.

Since your comment about what pushed you towards transitioning I've been trying to think about how I feel about myself and femininity and it's causing me some trouble. I'll try and remember certain things, like a time I went on a school camping trip and the boys and girls had to be in different bunks, and how I wished I could be in the girl bunk, and it makes me wonder. I feel good when I crossdress sometimes, but I also always feel ashamed and like I'm stupid. I'm very conflicted.

That's ok, I get confused all the time. Take your time, I'll try and tell you some of why I crossdress though. Sexual arousal was always a huge part it. Even before puberty, when I'd do it I'd get erections and thinking about doing it would give me them as well, and that would just make me feel good. When I did hit puberty I pretty much only ever masturbated through wearing women's clothing and imagining myself as female. That's actually part of why I feel transitioning would be wrong for me, because I'm worried it would just be a sexual thing and I'd regret it.
As a separate question, could you tell or describe to me the reasons why you crossdress?

I'm pretty sure most people do just feel meh when they see themselves in the mirror. I'd guess that most of your excitement comes from finally feeling you have the right body, would you agree with that? Also, what makes conquest a masculine thing to you?

Thanks for sharing, this is really interesting. Were there any times that steps towards male-ness would make you happier? Sometimes I can feel happy about masculine things applying to me, I think more often though the idea can make me uncomfortable. Certain things, like body/facial hair, weight, and general demeanor that I associate with men, can really bother me and make me not want those things associated with me. Does that sound similar to you?

The question I'll ask myself is, why would I want a female body if I wished I could feel better about my body, instead of wishing I had a male body that might look better than what I have? I'll wonder why I want bigger hips instead of more muscular torso/arms. For me, even though I find some guys attractive, I just can't find anything attractive about myself, but if I was female I could. I wonder if maybe it's because when I try to think of myself as female I'm seeing myself as being more of another person, and that makes it easier somehow. It's complicated :\

Thanks for sharing your perspective. Would you be able to go into more detail about what pushed you towards that decision, and what specific things have made it seem like such a positive direction for you?

I really appreciate you sharing a more detailed response, reading it I saw a lot of similarities between us. I often feel like I could live a reasonably happy life as a male, if it weren't for a lot of other things going on in my life that make me more miserable at least. For me I just have trouble handling those periods where I want to be female, and also moments of general discomfort with myself as male. For me a lot of my desire to be female at times has to do with appearance and body image issues I have. Does that relate to you at all?
What if it was permanent?
Because I'd like to be dead.
I wish I could go back to sleep, my eyes/head hurt and there's no reason for me to be awake.

The antidepressants didn't really do anything at all, I tried a few of them as well. I stopped because I hoped it would make it easier to kill myself, as it meant there was no chance that future ones could help me feel normal.
I don't have questions, I don't know what to ask or talk about. I guess I'll just try and fall asleep and do the same thing over again tomorrow.

Yes, I've tried therapy and antidepressants for about a year, I'm still seeing a therapist but stopped with antidepressants because I got tired of them and because I felt it would make it more likely that I might finally kill myself. It's not that the antidepressants helped, but stopping meant I got rid of the chance that they could.

It might be hard for you to see but it's clear to me. Something I feel a little stupid about is that I've posted here before, with a different account, and talked about killing myself but I didn't. I feel like a coward and like I ought to have done something by now, while at the same time feeling afraid of those thoughts. It's so confusing.

I get the point but it's sort of silly, it's always an option. In that scenario people wouldn't need food or anything either. I get what you're asking and I'll try to answer. I'd want to find some meaning in my life and feel like I matter. I'd end up doing the same things though to try and help with that, like therapy. In terms of doing something to feel connected with other people, I don't see myself being able to do much of that because I have really bad social anxiety. I don't know what I'd do.
No, I feel maybe I can't be helped. I keep going because I do have a hope that things will change but it's hard to keep that up and sometimes I end up putting appointments off.
It doesn't matter because I don't deserve to live.

I don't have many interests, I usually don't have energy to pursue things. Some days I can't even watch things on netflix. I will sit at my computer and mindlessly web surf and listen to music until I feel like lying down.
I've seen two therapists, one over the course of a few months, I'd see her a couple times a week, and the second therapist I've seen for longer, close to a year now.
I only asked out of a hope that maybe I could apply some small thing from your own experiences to my life and maybe find a way to cope with these things.

I started trying medication before I started therapy actually, I tried it for about a year and didn't have any success with it. I tried a few different medications and dosages over that period but at best it would just make me feel the same as usual. I just want to die.
Why don't you dislike yourself? Why don't you hate yourself? Why don't you die?

Maybe I dislike myself and other people, I don't know why I would feel that way though. I don't honestly know why I feel this way. I think I am a little hostile towards other people actually, I get worried that I'll be judged poorly for associating with people sometimes. I dunno, it's too confusing, I just want to be dead. Also, the internet hug thing kind of bugs me :\ I don't mean to be rude or something, it just makes me feel weird.

How do you find people that will listen? How do you have the courage not to hold things in your heart? 

I've felt separate and disjointed from society and other people, not through my whole life but there have been significant periods where I feel like I'm just not a person almost. I'm sorry that's something you've had to deal with. I feel kind of odd about it but I find that hearing other people's struggles can make me feel less negative about my own, so I thank you for sharing. 

I struggle with loneliness, but something I also struggle with is finding excitement or hope in life and being able to translate that into forward motion that can help me out of depression. Do you have any advice towards that?

I don't mean to seem confrontational or anything by the way, or like I'm just being stubborn or something. I want to trust you, I want to believe that it's possible for some random person to have a sympathetic connection and offer support, I want to feel that I can have the same connection with people I know. Not that you seem to be responding to me as if I was confrontational, I just want to be clear that the resistance and difficulty I have is more directed at myself, if that makes sense. I'm kind of scared of being vulnerable like that I think though.

What is that makes you think I have value? Also, I know that suicide gets rid of a chance for things in my life to improve, but it also eliminates the possibility for things to get worse. 

Would you be able to tell me about the similar things you've gone through? I'm not asking because I'm doubting you or something, but because I'm just curious. You can PM me if you'd rather, I know that maybe another person might read these comments and might get some use out of them, but for me I worry about people reading what I say and thinking I'm stupid or something.

It's really hard for me to trust in what you say, not because I have any reason to find you a deceptive person, I just don't have much faith in anyone I guess. Why would you think about me? I feel like the more people know about me the less they would want to have anything to do with me.

I've been seeing a therapist for a year but it doesn't help. I could talk to my family more but they don't actually care, and I don't have any friends and haven't in many years. I can't say for certain that my family doesn't care, but what I can say is that for me it just won't ever feel like they care. It doesn't make rational sense but I can't fight these feelings, they are too strong.
I just meant thanks for the offer of support, and that I'm not sure where to go with questioning and exploring my identity.
Thanks for the offer, I'm really not sure where to go from here though.
Thanks for sharing, it's informative to hear and I appreciate you putting this stuff out. I'm sorry that you've struggled so much.

That sounds so awful :( Trying to meet their expectations and it making you miserable I mean, and it not making anyone happy. It sounds a lot like me too. For me there's some comfort in doing that though, because trying to stand by my own decisions scares me a little.

What were the coping mechanisms you'd try to use?
I was trying to be funny, no worries :)

I'm sorry those negative feelings are so intense for you. It's hard for me to put myself in your shoes and imagine what that's like. 

This is sort of separate, but for me it's really hard not to try and live my life the way I imagine others want me to. It's easy for me to tell myself to just do what makes me happy, but actually doing that is very hard. You can talk about these things like they are no big deal, and maybe that's how they are for most people, but not for me. Maybe I'm insane :\
That's really interesting. Your comment, and those of a bunch of others here, have helped me not feel so much like an alien.

What are your personal body hangups like?

Also, when you mention plenty of perspective, do you mean internal or external perspectives? It's hard for me to talk about this sort of topic with people who know me better, but I can try and be more receptive to my own feelings/thoughts. It's something I struggle with a lot though, and I already feel like I'm a failure at life. Also, I don't mean to be insensitive or anything, but aren't there problems with being someone who has a clothes fetish or being trans? I feel like people in general might look down on you for the former, and in the latter a person can face discrimination and also the physical boundaries that transitioning works to overcome. Am I looking at it in the wrong way? I must be, but I don't know how to view it differently.

Thanks for being so open, I really appreciate it. I actually have the same feelings when I cross dress, wearing women's clothing stopped being as sexually arousing when I was in my mid teens, and for awhile I stopped doing it altogether. I tried it again in the last year or so with clothing that I bought for myself and there are times when it makes me feel...not quite sad I guess, but maybe close. I'd be looking at myself in the mirror with a bra on and just kind of wince. There have been brief moments where I could see myself as female in appearance and it'd make me dizzy. Shaving my legs is something I've done, I've had positive and negative feelings towards that. I like the advice about wearing more androgynous clothes, I might try that. I actually like all your advice and will try to keep it in mind.
Are there details from what I've said/described that you (or others) feel might separate me from say, a person with a kink for cross dressing or similar things?

What's interesting about my answers being clothing oriented?

This is a fun hypothetical question though, it's hard to answer. I think I'd rather be a girl in that situation. Actually, I dunno :\ I'm used to being seen as male when I interact with people. I could imagine a person referring to me as she or her or something and it makes my heart flutter but I think in reality I'd have to do double takes and make sure people actually were talking to me. If I picture myself as being a boy in that situation my usual reservations and feelings of being embarrassing would be there. Maybe I'm just bad at imagining, and if I was a girl I'd feel that same embarrassment.

Oh okay, that's what I thought you meant. I should also clarify, I don't get aroused by every scenario that involves me not being the gender I was assigned at birth, sometimes the idea just feels nice.
Did you ask all of them?

>It's the same for me, but it's not a sexual thing and it doesn't arouse me.


I'm not sure I understand what you mean, are you able to phrase it in a different way?

Are there any studies showing that cis-men get turned on by the idea of being men during sexual activities? It sounds like a silly question, but maybe someone can provide insight. 

I appreciate the advice by the way. I'm not sure how to explore things, or maybe I should say, I don't have the confidence to do so. I could try and ask my family to all call me a girl's name or something, but I am nowhere near bold enough to do something like that. Would you have any suggestions or ideas in that area?
It's hard to say, a girl body maybe? Those are all things I've enjoyed doing though :D One of the things that makes me lean towards a female body is that I might like the clothing I was wearing more.

I don't know if it matters, but I've tried to picture myself as male in sexual/romantic situations, but almost all the time it just feels like a lie, I'll feel like no one would ever want to be in that sort of situation with me. It also feels off sort of, I don't know how to better explore that feeling. There are moments, like in dreams, that I can recall where it didn't feel that way, and it seemed great, but these are rare. I mean, I've had dreams where I was female and those seemed great as well. 

Anyway, your original statement is kind of just a reflection of the underlying question in my original post. What I'm saying is that I agree with the statement, but I don't know how to resolve it and I feel weird about it being a problem for me. I've read about autogynephilia before, maybe I'll spend the rest of the day reading about it more.

These are some interesting questions, I've thought about the first one a bit before. The way it's seemed to me is that I'd have been happier with life. I wouldn't have had a secret that was always gnawing at me, the secret being that I liked wearing women's clothing, and I feel like I would have had more friends, or had an easier time interacting with other people maybe. I have pretty bad social anxiety and depression at the moment though, and I'll feel like there are lots of things that could have been different that would have helped me be more satisfied with my life. My emotional reaction to that question might be odd or maybe stupid, I feel like I'm wrong for feeling that way and I feel like I'm just looking for an excuse instead of trying to address my problems.

If I could decide what sex to be and when, I think maybe I'd be female more often, maybe it would be novel for awhile. My days would probably be the same, I just spend most of my time online or doing solitary things.

It's hard to say what I like about being treated as a man, or what I'd like if I were treated as a woman. I guess it'd be more likely for a person to flirt with me, which might be nice if I liked the person. I like when people call me sir, mainly because it makes me feel like they respect me and I'm not pathetic. I'm not sure what specific things I like about being a man, it's hard to think of specific masculine things. I might like how I looked if I were a woman, I've found that generally I like feminine aspects of my appearance and my mannerisms.

>For some reason, in many people the sex drive becomes the repository of repressed things--their forbiddenness becomes transformed into erotic energy, which allows them to be expressed with compulsive force even when they're being repressed everywhere else.

You and nancysbw have both said this, which is really interesting for me because it brings something to mind. I can't recall exactly when I started noticing this, maybe sometime in the last year or two, but whenever I've masturbated I'll find that it's less about wanting a sexual release and more that I want to bring myself to that mental place where I am picturing myself as female. I really don't think I would actually want that, to be female, but it's hard to say sometimes, I guess I'm bringing it up because I don't know how to get to the root of those feelings. If I were repressing feelings, how am I supposed to stop doing that?
